tagline: Railways and lumber shaped Crandon; a trail follows Lily's old tracks.
intro: Hiles lies on Highway 32 north-northwest of Crandon, a city on the northern shore of Metonga Lake. Farther south, Highway 55 connects Crandon with Lily, where the Lily River meets the Wolf.

Rail service helped shape these communities: a spur reached Crandon at the turn of the twentieth century, and lumber companies recruited loggers from Kentucky. At Lily, the railway operated until 2001, when its tracks were removed; the grade became the Wolf River State Trail.

Travel south from Hiles toward Crandon and the lake, then take Highway 55 toward Pickerel and Lily. Across the town of Langlade, the Wolf flows northwest to southeast within the Fox River watershed leading to Green Bay. Hollister also lies on Highway 55.

moments.title: Hiles
moments.text: Hiles takes its name from lumber baron F. P. Hiles. Its post office opened in 1903 and closed in 1968. The community is on Highway 32, ten miles north-northwest of Crandon.

moments.title: Crandon
moments.text: Kentucky is part of Crandon's story: lumber companies recruited settlers and loggers from there as rail service reached the timber country. A company sawmill was even moved here from Glasgow, Kentucky. Crandon's population rose from 800 to more than 2,400 in a few years. The city incorporated in 1909, and much of its building stock dates from that period. The annual Kentuck Days Festival celebrates that Kentucky ancestry. Although lumber's role has diminished, logging companies continue working in the nearby Nicolet National Forest, and logging remains among the city's major industries.

moments.title: Lily
moments.text: At Lily, two rivers meet and two state highways cross. The community stands on the eastern side of the Wolf River, joined here by the Lily River from the northeast. Wisconsin Central Ltd, successor here to the Soo Line, operated the railway through Lily until 2001. The tracks were removed that year, and the grade is now the Wolf River State Trail. Lily is also a junction for area snowmobile and ATV trails. Highways 52 and 55 meet here: one heads toward Wabeno and Antigo, the other links Crandon with Shawano.
